hints.hint: Uses a try/except instead of pytest.raises and puts quote and breakdown in the same try block.
hints.why: The test can finish without an assertion if neither call raises, and an exception from the first call prevents exercising the second.

hints.hint: Compares the 15-minute result with a separate zero-duration quote rather than naming a literal free amount.
hints.why: The oracle is indirect; a shared incorrect result could satisfy the comparison.

hints.hint: The name says “same_night”, but its dates run from March 9 to March 11.
hints.why: The scenario encoded by the inputs conflicts with the stated behavior, making the test purpose misleading.

hints.hint: The expected value is a repeat of the identical quote call with identical arguments.
hints.why: This self-comparison is structurally tautological and provides no independent expected outcome.

hints.hint: The name promises a six-euro rate, while the test structure only compares a night quote against a daytime quote.
hints.why: The test name is more specific than its oracle and the relational comparison does not document the required amount.

hints.hint: Introduces a naive/UTC-aware datetime mix and expects TypeError.
hints.why: Timezone compatibility is not a PARK-6 requirement; the test name and marker make an out-of-scope implementation behavior look like tariff coverage.

hints.hint: Uses `receipt in (receipt, "FREE")`.
hints.why: Including the observed value itself makes the membership condition tautological.

hints.hint: It is marked PARK-10 although its name and nonzero input concern the formatted non-free branch.
hints.why: The traceability marker does not match the requirement being described; PARK-9 is the positive-amount receipt requirement.

hints.hint: The name claims the exact FREE receipt, but the check is only absence of the substring `EUR`.
hints.why: The stated behavior is stronger than the test's surface-level oracle.

hints.hint: Uses a negative amount despite receipt requirements only specifying zero and positive amounts.
hints.why: The case is outside the documented input partition, so it is weak evidence for the PARK-9 marker.

hints.hint: The title says the cap is reached after seven hours, while the first scenario is exactly seven hours and is paired with a just-over-seven-hours scenario.
hints.why: The wording is imprecise about the boundary the test is intended to cover.

hints.hint: Patches the private helper `parkfee.tariff._hourly_charge` and compares the result to the mock's return value.
hints.why: The test is coupled to an internal implementation seam and its title describes a tariff rule that the mocked helper bypasses.

hints.hint: It is marked PARK-5 and named as a multi-day test, but explicitly sets `lost_ticket=True`.
hints.why: Lost-ticket precedence belongs to PARK-8, so the marker and name obscure what behavior the scenario targets.

hints.hint: The title claims capping, but the test uses only less-than comparisons against uncapped arithmetic.
hints.why: This is a weak oracle for the exact PARK-4 cap and would allow many undercharges.

hints.hint: Checks Decimal exponent/representation rather than a stated tariff outcome.
hints.why: PARK-3 specifies the charge, not a Decimal storage-format contract; this is implementation-oriented coverage.

hints.hint: The three-hour, same-day scenario does not visibly distinguish counting from entry time from simple duration-based calculation.
hints.why: The scenario title promises a specific counting origin that the supplied case does not isolate.

hints.hint: It is marked PARK-7 and named for validation, but also sets `lost_ticket=True`.
hints.why: The scenario is dominated by the PARK-8 lost-ticket rule, so the marker/name are misleading validation traceability.

hints.hint: The PARK-8-marked, lost-ticket-named test never passes `lost_ticket=True`.
hints.why: Its data does not surface the condition named by either the requirement marker or test name.

hints.hint: Asserts the complete `repr` string of a Breakdown, including enum and timedelta representation details.
hints.why: This is brittle representation coupling rather than a stable public-value check.

hints.hint: The name says “forty euros”, but the structure compares the fee to `Decimal(fee)` and to another identical quote rather than to `Decimal("40.00")`.
hints.why: Both comparisons are self-derived and do not visibly encode the named required fee.

hints.hint: Patches private `_validated_free` to return True.
hints.why: The test is implementation-coupled and does not exercise the three-hour validation boundary advertised by its name.

hints.hint: The suite copies every `verifies` marker into JUnit user properties.
hints.why: This is positive traceability infrastructure: requirement IDs are retained in collected test results, though the mis-marked tests above reduce its reliability.

hints.hint: The marker definition requires requirement IDs in `ID~REV` form and strict markers are enabled.
hints.why: This is a positive surface signal of intentional, machine-checkable requirement-to-test traceability.
